purpose: Provider-neutral canonical CRM contract plus Stage 3.5 metadata-driven capability recovery runtime owned by GBAP/GBAP.

createRequestRule.businessId: GBAP durable ID; required and provider-neutral
createRequestRule.relatedBusinessIds: GBAP durable IDs; resolved by GBAP mapping layer before provider invocation
createRequestRule.opportunityLifecycle: The bounded canonical create slice supports OPEN Opportunity creation; OPEN requires a mapped Account business ID.

operationalExtensions.deleteRule: Canonical compatibility delete remains provider-backed and mapping-aware. Stage 3.5 runtime normal delete uses recoverable soft-delete semantics; permanent destroy is a separate high-privilege operation.

metadataRuntimeExtensions.purpose: Recover provider-supported CRM objects, fields, relations, views, record-page layouts and record lifecycle without exposing provider credentials or durable provider IDs to the browser.
metadataRuntimeExtensions.browserIdentityRule: Browser-facing runtime uses objectKey, fieldKey and GBAP durable businessId. Provider metadata and record IDs are translation-only server state.
metadataRuntimeExtensions.dynamicObjectRule: Active provider custom objects are recoverable without creating a new handwritten GBAP Surface. Dynamic records receive a GBAP business namespace and durable mapping.
metadataRuntimeExtensions.fieldRule: Only active policy-permitted fields are rendered; system/read-only fields cannot be written through the generic runtime.
metadataRuntimeExtensions.relationRule: Relations cross the browser boundary as related businessId + objectKey and are translated to provider record IDs server-side.
metadataRuntimeExtensions.viewRule: Provider Table/Kanban/Calendar view field visibility, ordering, filters, sorting and grouping are normalized into provider-neutral view metadata.
metadataRuntimeExtensions.layoutRule: Provider record-page tabs/widgets are normalized; GBAP may substitute governed native widgets for files/mail/calendar while preserving the user-facing record-page capability.
metadataRuntimeExtensions.lifecycleRule: Normal runtime delete is recoverable soft delete; restore is available to authorized users; permanent destroy is restricted to GBAP super-admin authority.

normalizedResultRule: Adapters return provider data only to the GBAP server boundary. GBAP adds durable businessId and strips provider record/metadata IDs before runtime records reach browser business callers.
canonicalExportRule: crm.v1.snapshot.export returns contractVersion, sourceProvider, accounts, contacts and opportunities in normalized provider-neutral shapes.
compatibilityRule: Historical specialized CRM surfaces and provider-specific PoU capabilities remain available during Stage 3.5 migration. They are compatibility/focused workflows, not a reason to hide metadata-supported provider business capability.
nonClaims: Metadata-driven recovery does not expose Twenty login, credentials, workspace administration or billing to normal users.
Provider-native AI does not become the GBAP AI authority merely because it exists in the provider.
Deep workflow/object/layout builders remain permission-gated managed capabilities; GBAP does not duplicate the provider workflow engine.
Stage 3.5 does not weaken provider replaceability or the GBAP identity/authorization boundary.
